alignment.note: Greek uses imperfect indicative ἐθαύμαζεν; Syriac employs periphrastic construction ܡܬܕܡܪ ܗܘܐ (participle + auxiliary 'was'); Vulgate mirrors Greek with simple imperfect mirabatur. All three express continuous past action, but Syriac uses analytic verbal construction typical of its aspectual system.

Greek ἀπιστίαν ('unbelief, lack of faith') and Vulgate incredulitatem align semantically. Syriac ܒܚܣܝܪܘܬ ܗܝܡܢܘܬܗܘܢ literally renders 'in the deficiency of their faith,' using ܚܣܝܪܘܬ (deficiency, lack) + ܗܝܡܢܘܬܐ (faith) in construct state, presenting faith as deficient rather than absent—a substantive theological nuance distinguishing partial from total unbelief.

Greek περιῆγεν (imperfect of περιάγω, 'was going around') and Vulgate circuibat (imperfect of circumeo) use synthetic verb forms. Syriac again employs periphrastic ܡܬܟܪܟ ܗܘܐ (participle + auxiliary), maintaining aspectual consistency with the previous clause—a stylistic preference rather than semantic divergence.

Greek κώμας ('villages') and Syriac ܩܘܪܝܐ (villages) align precisely. Vulgate castella ('small fortified towns, hamlets') represents a Latin lexical choice emphasizing fortification or settlement size, though functionally equivalent in rural Galilean context—likely reflecting Roman administrative terminology.

Greek κύκλῳ (adverb, 'around, in a circuit') appears post-verbally. Vulgate splits the concept into prepositional phrase in circuitu ('in a circuit'), maintaining the sense but using analytic Latin construction. Syriac omits explicit adverbial modifier, the circuitous motion being implicit in the verb ܡܬܟܪܟ itself (from root ܟܪܟ, 'to go around')—a case of lexical incorporation.

Greek uses present participle διδάσκων ('teaching') in attendant circumstance construction. Vulgate employs gerund docens with identical function. Syriac uses temporal particle ܟܕ ('while, as') + active participle ܡܠܦ, making the simultaneity syntactically explicit through subordinating conjunction—a characteristic Syriac strategy for rendering Greek circumstantial participles.
